contract.question: Will the Oklahoma City Thunder win the 2024-2025 NBA Championship?
contract.resolutionEvidence: Polymarket page shows End Date Jun 23, 2025, Outcome proposed Yes, No dispute, Final outcome Yes; NBA sources confirm Oklahoma City won the Finals.
contract.contractGap: Exact Gamma event/market/token metadata and retained hourly history are captured in the sports evidence folder; scored measurements are reproducible with evaluate-thunder.mjs.

cards.title: Thunder open by beating Denver 102–87
cards.claim: Oklahoma City beat the reigning MVP's Nuggets 102–87 in Denver; Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 28 and Chet Holmgren had 25 with 14 rebounds.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: A road win over a leading Western rival immediately raises the team's ceiling and validates the young core.

source.role: NBA/AP game recap; page timestamp is timezone-naive

cards.title: Chet Holmgren suffers a pelvic fracture
cards.claim: The Thunder announced Holmgren sustained a right iliac wing fracture and would receive a return-to-play update in eight to ten weeks after the November 10 loss to Golden State.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: A core two-way starter's injury changes the team's playoff ceiling and frontcourt depth, even with a return expected during the season.

source.role: NBA News Services; retained page update timestamp

cards.title: Thunder finish 68–14 with NBA's best record
cards.claim: Oklahoma City beat New Orleans 115–100 to finish 68–14, the best record in the NBA and the best regular season in franchise history.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: The finished record confirms the strongest available baseline and home-court advantage through the playoffs; home court had been clinched earlier, so this is not treated as a newly secured benefit.

source.role: NBA/AP contemporary game recap; page timestamp is timezone-naive

cards.title: Thunder sweep Memphis in the first round
cards.claim: Oklahoma City completed a 4–0 sweep of Memphis with a 117–115 Game 4 win and became the first team into the second round.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: A clean opening-series win removes a playoff branch while demonstrating the top seed can close tight games.

source.role: NBA/AP game recap; page timestamp is timezone-naive

cards.title: Thunder reach the NBA Finals
cards.claim: Oklahoma City beat Minnesota 124–94 to win the Western Conference finals 4–1 and advance to the NBA Finals.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: Only one best-of-seven series remained, sharply reducing uncertainty in the championship contract.

source.role: Thunder official release; exact retained publication timestamp

ending.text: Oklahoma City defeated Indiana 4–3 in the 2025 NBA Finals, winning Game 7 103–91 on June 22, 2025. Polymarket's Thunder YES contract resolved YES.

contract.question: Which team will win the 2025 MLB World Series? (Los Angeles Dodgers outcome)
contract.resolutionEvidence: Polymarket page reports World Series Champion 2025, rules tied to the team that wins the 2025 World Series, and Los Angeles Dodgers as the final leader; MLB confirms Dodgers won Game 7 5–4 in 11 innings.
contract.contractGap: The public page and slug are exact enough for editorial review, but this packet does not yet contain the selected outcome's Gamma/CTF IDs or retained historical price series. The two-outcome World Series Winner market is a separate, later contract and should not be substituted without review.

cards.title: Dodgers sign Roki Sasaki
cards.claim: Los Angeles signed 23-year-old Japanese right-hander Roki Sasaki after a three-team finalist process; he had a 2.35 ERA and 129 strikeouts in 111 NPB innings in 2024.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: Adding a high-upside starter to a defending champion's rotation strengthens the perceived depth of the title favorite.

source.role: MLB official press release; page date only, exact time to be captured

cards.title: Sasaki pauses throwing with no return timeline
cards.claim: The Dodgers said Sasaki stopped playing catch and had no timeline to resume, prompting the club to plan for life without him for the 2025 season.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: The highly anticipated rotation addition became uncertain, reducing depth and increasing reliance on other injured starters.

source.role: MLB/Dodgers report; exact publication time to be captured

cards.title: Dodgers add deadline depth
cards.claim: On July 31 the Dodgers acquired Brock Stewart, Paul Gervase, Adam Serwinowski, Ben Rortvedt and Alex Call in deadline transactions, while trading Dustin May.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: A multi-player deadline reshaped pitching and roster depth for the stretch run, a direct signal about championship intent.

source.role: MLB official transactions; date shown, exact time unavailable

cards.title: Dodgers clinch the NL West
cards.claim: Los Angeles beat Arizona 8–0 to clinch a fourth straight NL West title and its 12th division title in 13 years.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: The division title secures a playoff berth and confirms a season-long contender despite a less dominant regular-season record than expected.

source.role: MLB official recap; page date shown, exact time unavailable

cards.title: Dodgers sweep Brewers to win the NL pennant
cards.claim: Los Angeles beat Milwaukee 5–1 in NLCS Game 4; Shohei Ohtani hit three home runs, struck out 10 and pitched six scoreless innings as the Dodgers completed a four-game sweep.
cards.whyCouldMoveOdds: The defending champion reached the World Series with its star performing as a two-way ace, reducing the title path to one series.

source.role: MLB official recap; page date shown, exact time unavailable

ending.text: The Dodgers defeated Toronto 5–4 in 11 innings in Game 7 on November 1, 2025, becoming MLB's first repeat champions since 1998–2000. The Polymarket Dodgers outcome resolved as the winner.
